title: Browns Ferry and the fight against eelgrass
summary: Opportunities to improve maintenance efficiency can arise unexpectedly at nuclear power plants. At Browns Ferry in Athens, Ala., one opportunity arose when an unexpected surge of nonnative eelgrass in the Tennessee River clogged the cooling water intake, prompting the shutdown of two reactors and the derating of a third to about 78 percent power. Power plant engineers said the single surge reportedly cost the Tennessee Valley Authority about $15 million–$20 million in revenue. A 2026 report from the International Atomic Energy Agency said the same incident resulted in a production loss of roughly 0.5 terawatt-hours.

title: Three universities launch nuclear education consortium
summary: Three universities are coming together to meet the emerging need to fill gaps in the nuclear workforce by developing microcredentials and immersive training tools that bring nuclear education to a broader group of students. Arizona State University, Purdue University, and the University of Tennessee–Knoxville announced they have launched the New Nuclear Academic Consortium.

title: NRC allows alternate approach to removing tilted fuel assembly at Palisades
summary: Roughly two weeks after Holtec submitted a license amendment request (LAR) following a fuel loading incident at the Palisades nuclear power plant, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission approved Holtec’s emergency request to remove a tilted fuel assembly from the power plant’s reactor vessel using custom-made equipment.

title: Sweden’s Studsvik Signs ‘Landmark’ Spent Nuclear Fuel Agreement With Norway
summary: Sweden-based nuclear services company Studsvik has signed what it called a “landmark” agreement to manage Norway’s legacy spent nuclear fuel. The agreement with Norwegian Nuclear Decommissioning (NND), the Norwegian state agency responsible for decommissioning the country’s nuclear facilities, runs until 2055 and has an estimated contractual minimum value of about SEK 875m (€78m, $88m) and a potential total value for Studsvik of SEK 3-4bn. It covers transport, treatment of waste to meet long-term storage requirements and the interim storage of spent fuel from Norway’s former research reactors at Halden and Kjeller.

title: Maritime Nuclear Startup Bluecore Buys First Uranium For Nuclear Plants On Barges
summary: Bluecore Energy, the Long Beach, US-based floating nuclear power startup, has bought its first supply of uranium hexafluoride (UF6), a low-enriched 4.95% blend of U-235 suitable for a commercial nuclear power installation. The material is being held at a US nuclear fuel facility outside the state of California while Bluecore advances its plans for future fuel fabrication, testing and validation. UF6 is the required form of uranium during the enrichment stage of the nuclear fuel cycle. During the fuel fabrication stage, the UF6 is converted into uranium dioxide, or UO2, which can then be fabricated into fuel pellets and assembled into nuclear fuel. The purchase follows Bluecore’s recent $50m (€44m) seed financing.
